description: Aux is a team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Ankara. We aim to work together to develop a solution to our chosen challenge using NASA’s open data.
summary: AstroMatch AI is an interactive platform that helps users discover Earth locations with terrain similar to regions on Mars and the Moon. Using NASA and Copernicus elevation data, it compares slope, relief, roughness, and landscape shape through explainable similarity analysis. The AstroGrid interface displays planetary and Earth terrains side by side with synchronized 3D views and feature-level comparisons. Users can explore selected areas as an astronaut, drive a six-wheel rover under planet-specific gravity, and practice a simulated spacecraft landing. An Analog Profile presents environmental context, including available surface temperature, vegetation, and water or ice evidence, separately from the terrain score. By displaying data sources, missing observations, and uncertainty, AstroMatch AI supports planetary research, analog field studies, and space education while helping users understand both the similarities and differences between worlds.
details:
AstroMatch AI helps users identify Earth locations with terrain similar to selected regions on Mars and the Moon. It processes NASA MOLA and LOLA elevation data alongside SRTM and Copernicus DEM products, extracting slope, relief, roughness, and landscape-shape features. Comparable features are combined into explainable similarity scores.

The AstroGrid interface presents synchronized 3D terrain comparisons, ranked Earth candidates, and feature-level explanations. Its Analog Profile separates environmental evidence, including available MODIS temperature and vegetation data, from topographic ranking. Users can explore selected parcels as an astronaut, operate a six-wheel rover under planet-specific gravity, and practice a fictional spacecraft landing.

We developed the platform using Python, FastAPI, NumPy, Rasterio, and PyArrow for data processing and backend services; TypeScript, React, Three.js, and React Three Fiber for visualization; Rapier for rover physics; and Docker for deployment.

The project’s creativity lies in connecting quantitative terrain matching with interactive exploration and mission-oriented evidence. Our team considered source resolution, consistent analysis scales, measurement support, missing observations, and uncertainty. Unknown values remain explicit, and generated scenery is distinguished from measured terrain. The intended impact is to make planetary data more accessible for analog field studies, exploratory research, and space education without presenting terrain similarity as mission suitability.
